analysis: The supplied units are head-side text of CHANGELOG.md (lines 5061-5475), historical release notes. The patch excerpt shows the only changed range is head 11-45, a new v0.10.13 candidate section, which falls outside the supplied head_text units. No executable code, configuration, workflow or threat-model YAML is changed in the visible evidence, so I found no security control altered by this PR. The two units contain only unchanged historical entries, and I did not re-assert pre-existing issues. They mention frozen legacy MDM cohort (T-036, T-052/T-055/T-057), SSD cache persistence and TTL (T-041/SEC-035), bounded non-streaming responses, and removal of caller-supplied top-level user/metadata/prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies. All of these describe earlier changes and are consistent with the threat model, which already says caller prompt_cache_key/user do not participate in cache scope. The new v0.10.13 text in the patch states a Gemma 4 loop-exit-thinking guard (#2040, default on, env kill switch DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING=0) and a cluster-pair start/stop fix (#2042). The excerpt is truncated and the underlying source changes are not supplied here, so I cannot assess them. Integration should check whether the code changes in other batches touch the following areas: T-010 (stop/cancel propagation for the pair start during download/load), T-008 (response encryption on the new loop-exit path), and TB-012/TB-007 (model-load and hold handling). The documentation-only changelog changes carry no verifiable security regression from the evidence available.
